Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 s=msg.split(label,1)[1]
 rows=[]
 for line in s.splitlines()[1:]:
  if not re.fullmatch(r'(?:[0-9] )*[0-9]',line): break
  rows.append(list(map(int,line.split())))
 return rows
di=grid_after('Demo pair 1 input (22x22):')
do=grid_after('Demo pair 1 output (22x22):')
test=grid_after('Test input (22x22):')
print(len(di),len(do),len(test),set(map(len,di)),set(map(len,do)))
(base/'task-215acdfb.json').write_text(json.dumps([{'input':di,'output':do}]))
program='''def transform(grid):
    h = len(grid)
    w = len(grid[0])
    colors = [v for row in grid for v in row]
    bg = max(set(colors), key=colors.count)
    blocks = []
    for r in range(h - 4):
        for c in range(w - 4):
            patch = [row[c:c+5] for row in grid[r:r+5]]
            border = patch[0] + patch[4] + [patch[i][0] for i in range(1,4)] + [patch[i][4] for i in range(1,4)]
            inner = [patch[i][j] for i in range(1,4) for j in range(1,4)]
            if len(set(border)) == 1 and border[0] != bg and len(set(inner)) == 1 and inner[0] != bg:
                blocks.append((r, c, patch))
    out = [[bg] * w for _ in range(h)]
    occupied = [[False] * w for _ in range(h)]
    for r, c, patch in sorted(blocks, reverse=True):
        nr = h - 5
        while any(occupied[nr+i][c+j] for i in range(5) for j in range(5)):
            nr -= 5
        for i in range(5):
            for j in range(5):
                out[nr+i][c+j] = patch[i][j]
                occupied[nr+i][c+j] = True
    return out
'''

    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])

    blocks = []
    for r in range(h - 4):
        for c in range(w - 4):
            p = [row[c:c+5] for row in grid[r:r+5]]
            border = p[0] + p[4] + [p[i][0] for i in range(1,4)] + [p[i][4] for i in range(1,4)]
            inner = [p[i][j] for i in range(1,4) for j in range(1,4)]

                blocks.append((r, c, p))
    out = [[bg] * w for _ in range(h)]
    occupied = [[False] * w for _ in range(h)]
    # Azure blocks fall left; red blocks fall right.
    for direction in (-1, 1):
        group = [b for b in blocks if b[2][0][0] == (8 if direction == -1 else 2)]

        for r, c, p in group:
